entries.name: Mount Gower

facts.claim: Mt Gower is Lord Howe's highest mountain at 875 m; the hike is a challenging eight-hour return trek of about 14 km with rope-assisted climbs and dizzying drops, rated one of Australia's best day walks.
Mt Gower is 4.5 km one way, difficult, and 'only accessible with a guide'; it 'must only be attempted with a licensed guide'.
Visitor access to Mt Gower is only permitted with a licensed guide (LHI Board).

Guided Mt Gower treks are run by Lord Howe Environmental Tours (Dean Hiscox, $200 per person) and Sea to Summit Expeditions (Jack Shick, veteran guide of 2,200+ walks, limited numbers, advance booking recommended).
The summit has misty cloud forest with Lord Howe woodhens and views over the southern end of the island.

entries.hours: Guided tours only; book ahead (about 8 hours return)

entries.name: Ball's Pyramid

facts.claim: Ball's Pyramid is 23 km southeast of the island, the world's tallest sea stack at 551 m and a site of some of Australia's most remarkable diving.
It is a popular spot for fishing charters and the only known place where the Ballina Angelfish can be seen scuba diving.
Recreational climbing there is prohibited, to protect the last wild population of the Lord Howe Island stick insect; climbers need Board permission.

Reef N Beyond runs a Ball's Pyramid / Lord Howe Island Expedition boat tour from A$250 (3.5 hours, ages 5 and up, up to 22 people, snorkelling optional); Dive Lord Howe runs Balls Pyramid dive trips (operates September to May).
Belle Chase offers an 8-hour shared Ball's Pyramid shelf fishing charter at $450 per person.

entries.hours: Boat tours and dive trips by booking, weather permitting

entries.name: Ned's Beach

facts.claim: At Ned's Beach, on the island's north-east, you can wade in and hand-feed fish (mullet, wrasse, garfish, silver-drummer, spangled emperor, kingfish); golden sand and calm water suit kids paddling or snorkelling over a fringing coral reef.
Masks, fins and snorkels can be hired at Ned's Beach, paid into an honesty box.
The Malabar Hill track starts off the side of the road just before the grassy section at Ned's Beach.
The fish-food dispenser takes $1 coins; Ned's Beach is the best-known snorkelling beach on the island.

entries.name: Malabar Hill

facts.claim: Red-tailed tropicbirds perform courting flights at Malabar between September and May; the cliffs host the world's largest nesting ground for the birds.
The two-hour return walk passes through palm forest with muttonbird burrows to panoramic views of Mt Lidgbird and Mt Gower to the south and the Admiralty Islands to the north.

Malabar Hill to Dawsons Point Ridge is 1.5 km one way, moderate: it starts at Ned's Beach, climbs a grassy slope to Pooles Lookout, reaches the 208 m summit and follows the cliff edge past Kim's Lookout.
Wikivoyage calls the climb to Malabar Ridge the most popular walk on the island.

entries.name: Old Settlement Beach

facts.claim: Weather-sculpted sandstone rocks dot the southern end of Old Settlement Beach; turtles are often sighted close to shore at mid to high tides.
It is a picture-perfect spot for picnics, swims and snorkelling with mountain views.
The Max Nichols Memorial Track to North Bay (1.5 km one way, moderate) starts at the picnic area at Old Settlement Beach.
Green turtles are best seen grazing on sea-grass off Old Settlement Beach; the Catalina Monument is next to the bike parking.

entries.name: Blinky Beach

facts.claim: Blinky Beach is an unspoilt, secluded beach for surfing, picnics, swimming in turquoise water and fishing.
The Transit Hill track continues about 0.5 km further to Blinky Beach; it is steep and slippery when wet. From the beach you can walk back along Lagoon Road.
Transit Hill walkers can walk across Blinky Beach along a narrow track to reach the lookout, then swim at Blinky Beach on return.
Wikivoyage describes the west side of the island as having several sandy surf beaches.

entries.name: North Bay

facts.claim: North Bay is a secluded beach at the north of the island accessible only by foot or water, with migratory seabirds, short walks to Mt Eliza and Old Gulch, and snorkelling with fish, turtles, stingrays and corals.
Snorkellers can explore the wreck of the Favourite, on the sea floor since 1965.
The picnic area at North Bay has toilets and barbecue facilities; the Max Nichols track from Old Settlement is 1.5 km one way, moderate.
Mt Eliza, from the North Bay picnic area, is closed September to March for nesting sooty terns; Old Gulch is a 0.3 km easy boardwalk walk from the picnic area.
Marine Adventures runs 3-hour North Bay Turtle and Nature Tours.

entries.name: Intermediate Hill

entries.name: Lord Howe Island Museum

facts.claim: The architect-designed Lord Howe Island Museum, opened in 2002, has displays on the island's World Heritage environment, community and history from 1788, and a skeleton of the extinct giant horned turtle Meiolania platyceps.
The Visitor Centre is in the Museum foyer; it also houses the Tropicbird Museum Shop and Coral Cafe.

Island directory: Museum and Gift Shop daily 9:00am-1:30pm (reduced hours June-August), corner of Lagoon Road and Middle Beach Road, +61 2 6563 2111; Visitor Centre Mon-Sat 9:00am-1:00pm, Sunday 10:00am-1:00pm.
